claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 initially has a high-temperature BCC state.
Cr atoms in the BCC matrix of Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 experience a negative local atomic stress.
Differences in local atomic stress drive chemical short-range ordering in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
Stress-mediated chemical short-range ordering produces local segregation during cooling.
Local segregation promotes the nucleation and growth of secondary phases during subsequent thermal exposure.
Slow cooling permits sufficient diffusion for substantial chemical short-range order to develop.
Moderate-temperature annealing permits further development of chemical short-range order.
Rapid quenching arrests diffusion and suppresses chemical short-range ordering.
Rapid quenching preserves Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 as a largely homogeneous BCC phase.
Cr-associated short-range ordering forms local clusters or ordered regions.
The local clusters or ordered regions cause compositional partitioning within the BCC matrix.
Compositionally partitioned regions act as nucleation sites for secondary phases.
Slow-cooled and annealed samples will show more chemical short-range order and local Cr enrichment or depletion than rapidly quenched samples.
Slow-cooled and annealed samples will contain more secondary phases than the rapidly quenched baseline.
The proposed mechanism should be inactive when cooling is too rapid or thermal exposure is too cold for atomic rearrangement.
Secondary phases should preferentially nucleate in regions having altered Cr concentration.

contradictions.description: The baseline is justified as homogeneous because quenching suppresses diffusion, but the experimental design subsequently gives that quenched baseline the same intermediate-temperature anneal intended to facilitate diffusion. Thus, the measured baseline is not necessarily the diffusion-arrested, uniform BCC state invoked in the prediction.
